commit.message:
test: deterministic stuck-cap and save-pool teardown tests (#3240, #3241) (#3243)

* test: age only the save under test past the stuck cap (#3240)

test_a_save_running_past_the_cap_escalates_at_once lowered the shared
MAX_EXPLICIT_STATE_SAVE_TIMEOUT_S to 0.0 after the first deferral. The
catch-up that deferral scheduled reads the same cap; under load it read
0.0, gave up on storage at once and sent a third, terminal error
([True, False, False]).

The test now backdates the hung save's own start time in
runtime._save_started_at, so the real _save_running_for check sees only
that save as running past the cap, and the shared cap is untouched.
Gate-offs: removing the product's stuck arm or the backdate both fail
the test with [True, True].

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: wait for deferred saves before the database flush (#3241)

The #3212 pool tests leave deferred saves (and their catch-up turns)
running past the test body: hung_store releases them only at teardown.
The released save then writes django_session on a pool thread while the
transactional teardown flushes the shared in-memory SQLite database, and
the shared cache answers 'database table is locked' (seen in the flush
of test_one_hung_store_write..., test_a_reconnect... and
test_a_navigation...).

Running on after the turn is the product's contract (#3212), so this is
a test fix: an autouse fixture records every spawned save and scheduled
catch-up and awaits them after hung_store releases, before the flush.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
fix: SSE and explicit-exposure follow-ups (#3211, #3212, #3221) (#3229)

* fix: route explicit views to the explicit commit whatever enable_state_snapshot says (#3211)

An explicit view with enable_state_snapshot=True went to the legacy
best-effort save on the event path, which acked a failed save and
bypassed ADR-038 E3. The event gate, the component-declaration gate and
the sticky-child predicate now require the legacy policy for the legacy
save; explicit views commit through commit_explicit_turn, as mount
already did. The legacy save refuses an explicit view before any write.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: changelog fragment for #3211

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: shut an SSE session down when its stream closes normally (#3221)

The stream's finally lingered and unregistered the session but never
called shutdown(), so the view's background work, waiters, upload temp
files and unregister hooks leaked. It now shuts its own session down
after the linger, under the dispatch lock so an in-flight turn finishes
first. A session already replaced by a same-owner reconnect is disposed
too: the reconnect mounted its own session and view, which are left
alone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: changelog fragment for #3221

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: re-check sticky children as the user the explicit mount runs as (#3212)

_build_live_redirect_request used the connect-time scope user for the
sticky-child auth re-check. After #3201 an explicit mount whose session
has vanished runs anonymous under a replacement session, so a
login_required sticky child survived into an anonymous page. The
re-check now goes through establish_mount_session with the runtime's
replacement map, so the redirect's mount reuses that replacement.
Legacy pages keep the scope user, as their mount does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: count only storage time against the legacy 150 ms save deadline (#3212)

_persist_state_after_event and _persist_sticky_child_after_event wrapped
several sync_to_async hops in one 150 ms wait_for, so on a busy sync
thread they dropped saves storage would have finished in milliseconds.
Both now run as one sync call through _run_explicit_save with the fixed
EVENT_STATE_SAVE_TIMEOUT_S: one Django-thread hop, the deadline counted
from when it starts, saves of one runtime ordered so a late save cannot
overwrite a newer one. A timeout or failure still only logs a warning.
The source and AST pins follow the new call shape.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: keep an abandoned save from blocking the loop at SSE request teardown (#3212)

Django serves each request inside a per-request ThreadSensitiveContext,
whose executor __aexit__ shuts down and waits for. An explicit save that
outran its deadline on the SSE event POST kept running on that executor,
so the event loop stopped until storage answered (and under sync
middleware the bridge thread was held). Saves made inside a request's
executors now run on a dedicated long-lived thread; WebSocket and
PooledHTTP slots are unchanged. The parallel path, a start_async task
spawned by the POST, is detached from the request's ThreadSensitiveContext
as well, not only from a sync bridge.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: changelog fragment for #3212

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: ruff-format the T012 hint that #3194 merged unformatted

The pre-push ruff-format hook checks the merged origin/main range and
refuses the push on this one quote style.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: address the #3229 review (save pool hygiene, B3 target policy, component commits)

- B1: every job on the request-scoped save threads is bracketed by
  close_old_connections(), as the worker pool does (#3095).
- B2: a bounded pool (min(32, 4 x CPUs)) instead of one thread, and the
  wait for a thread is bounded (10 s), so a queued save is deferred
  rather than stalling the turn. N3: SSE navigation and reconnect carry
  the old runtime's running save into the new runtime's ordering.
- B3: the live_redirect sticky re-check derives the user from the page
  being opened, not the page being left.
- I1/I2: every component event on an explicit view commits, after the
  waiters are notified, as on the view route.
- I3: a closed SSE stream waits at most 10 s for an in-flight POST.
- The late-save ordering test is now deterministic (review N5).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: correct the #3211/#3212/#3221 changelog fragments after the #3229 review

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: address the #3229 re-review (R1 start bound and stuck clock, R2 mounted view)

- R1: only request-scoped saves (the SSE/HTTP pool) get a wait-to-start
  bound, now 5 s, below the 10 s stuck cap; WebSocket saves keep #3206's
  unbounded queue wait. "Stuck" counts from when a save starts running
  (recorded per save future, so it follows a carried save), not from
  enqueue, so a first pool-queue deferral is transient.
- R2: the live_redirect sticky re-check decides from the view that will
  actually be mounted, chosen by the mount's own rule (the URL's view, or
  the client's view with a state_snapshot) and resolved through
  resolve_view_class; an unresolvable target re-checks as anonymous.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: #3212 changelog after the #3229 re-review

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
